name: faq
title: FAQ
description: A titled list of questions, each a Disclosure revealing its answer.

frame.summary: A heading, then a stack of Disclosures at reading measure. Optionally two-column (intro left, questions right) when wide.

components.name: disclosure
components.for: One per question; its headingLevel is base+1.

components.name: divider
components.for: Rules between questions, if Disclosure's set does not own them.

dependsOnFuture.interim: Disclosure's recipe already says the rule between stacked sections belongs to the set; until Divider exists the block draws a border-block-end with theme.border.default at border.default.

headingLevel.summary: The outline level of the section heading; each question is base+1; everything below it steps down from here.
use: The level the surrounding page gives this block — a template passes it explicitly.
dont: Choosing a level for its visual size. Size is the Heading component's `role`, a separate decision.
headingLevel.a11y: No default, for the reason Heading's `level` has none: only the caller knows the depth, and a skipped level breaks heading navigation for the whole page.

allowMultiple.summary: Whether several answers can be open at once.
dont: false as a space saver — closing an answer the reader was comparing against is a surprise.

behavior.summary: Each Disclosure owns its own open state; the block adds nothing but layout.

decisions.decision: Built on Disclosure, not a new accordion
decisions.why: Disclosure already implements the APG heading-plus-button pattern and requires a headingLevel; an FAQ is exactly that pattern repeated.
Find-in-page and screen-reader heading lists still reach the questions; opening all would make it a wall of text.

landmarks.label: aria-labelledby the block's own heading (the section heading)

obligations: Pass headingLevel = base + 1 to every Disclosure.

native.mapping: A help screen: a grouped list of questions; each row pushes (or expands to) the answer.

tokenGaps.need: A section-band vertical padding step larger than space.section for marketing rhythm
tokenGaps.interim: padding-block uses var(--rata-space-section) top and bottom. space.section is the only page-rhythm step and was sized for docs pages, not full-bleed marketing bands.
